title: Spool

---

A [`Spool`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool`) manages patches from memory, files, directories, or remote resources. File-backed spools scan metadata first and load arrays only when patches are accessed.

```{python}
import dascore as dc

spool = dc.get_example_spool()
```

# Data sources

Use [`dc.spool(...)`](`dascore.spool`) for any supported input:

```{python}
memory_spool = dc.spool([dc.get_example_patch()])
file_spool = dc.spool("examples://terra15_das_1_trimmed.hdf5")
```

Directory spools maintain an index for fast metadata queries. Call `update()` after files change.

```{python}
# Write example patches to a directory to get a usable path.
directory = dc.examples.spool_to_directory(dc.get_example_spool())
directory_spool = dc.spool(directory).update()
```

Remote [`UPath`](https://pypi.org/project/universal-pathlib/) resources use the same constructor; see [Working with remote patches](remote_patches.qmd). To keep the index elsewhere or open a spool from an index alone, see [Index location](large_archives.qmd#index-location); for `key=value` directory names, see [Path attributes](large_archives.qmd#path-attributes).

# Accessing patches

Indexing and iteration load patches. Slicing, integer arrays, and boolean masks return a new spool.

```{python}
first_patch = spool[0]
subset = spool[1:]

for patch in spool:
    ...
```

Integer arrays reorder patches and may repeat them; boolean arrays keep positions marked `True`:

```{python}
import numpy as np

reordered = spool[np.array([2, 0])]
mask = np.ones(len(spool), dtype=bool)
mask[1] = False
without_second = spool[mask]
```

Lists and pandas Series follow the same positional rules. Slicing remains lazy: it narrows the spool plan without loading selected arrays.

Rows from `get_contents()` align with spool positions, so a dataframe condition can select the same patches. Do not reuse a mask from a differently ordered spool.

```{python}
diverse = dc.get_example_spool("diverse_das")
rows = diverse.get_contents()
tagged = diverse[rows["tag"] == "some_tag"]
```

# Inspecting and selecting

Displaying a spool shows its patch count, coordinate extents, and tracks for distinct patch kinds. Large spools omit the expensive summary according to [`display_max_patches`](configuration.qmd).

A track groups patches with the same configured kind attributes and measures their span along time, or another available dimension. Single-kind spools omit redundant tracks because their overall extent already carries the same information. Tracks describe extents, not coverage; use [`get_coverage`](large_archives.qmd#gaps-and-coverage) for missing-data statistics.

```{python}
dc.get_example_spool("diverse_das")
```

[`Spool.get_contents`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.get_contents`) returns one metadata row per patch without loading its data array. File-backed rows include `source_path`, `source_format`, and `source_patch_key`.

```{python}
contents = diverse.get_contents()
contents[["time_min", "time_max", "source_format"]].head()
```

The dataframe is a realized relation, so requesting every row can be expensive for a very large remote archive. Apply `select` first whenever the index backend can push down the predicate.

[`Spool.select`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.select`) filters metadata and trims matching patches along coordinates.

```{python}
recent = diverse.select(time=("2020-01-03", ...))
sources = diverse.select(acquisition_key={"DAS2.R2D1..RAW", "DAS3.R2D1..RAW"})
glob_tags = diverse.select(tag="some*")
```

Coordinate selections both discard patches outside the range and trim intersecting patches. Attribute selections only filter rows. Collections, globs, and compiled regular expressions are accepted for string metadata. A glob means what SQLite's `GLOB` means, since that is what the index applies: `*` and `?` are wildcards, `[abc]` is a character class, and `[^abc]` negates one.

```{python}
import re

regex_tags = diverse.select(tag=re.compile(r"^some"))
```

## Unselect

[`Spool.unselect`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.unselect`) returns patches rejected by the same attribute selection.

```{python}
not_tagged = diverse.unselect(tag="some_tag")
```

Patch coordinates are excluded because complementing an interior range would split every patch; use [`Patch.unselect`](`dascore.Patch.unselect`) for that. Inventory coordinates are allowed; see [Inventory](inventory.qmd).

# Chunking

[`Spool.chunk`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.chunk`) lazily changes patch boundaries. It can merge contiguous patches, create fixed windows with overlap, or limit array size.

```{python}
from dascore.units import megabytes, s

windowed = spool.chunk(time=3 * s, overlap=1 * s, keep_partial=True)
merged = spool.chunk(time=None)
bounded = spool.chunk(time=1 * megabytes)
```

`overlap` accepts the same coordinate-unit, quantity, or data-size forms as the chunk length. `keep_partial=True` retains a shorter final window. Passing `time=None` asks DASCore to merge every contiguous compatible segment.

`chunk` takes lengths only. To request particular absolute windows, pass an `(n, 2)` array to `select` or `cut`. `select` returns each matching source piece separately; `cut` joins the pieces of each window as `chunk` joins patches, so a window crossing files gives one patch, and a gap leaves fragments labelled by the window's row. Rows stay in input order, including overlaps and duplicates, and a window running past the data keeps the samples it holds. Neither loads measurement arrays until a patch is asked for.

```{python}
small = dc.spool(dc.get_example_patch().select(distance=(0, 9)))
windows = np.array([[2, 4], [6, 8]])
source_pieces = small.select(distance=windows)
cut = small.cut(distance=windows)
assert len(source_pieces) == len(cut) == 2
assert cut.get_contents()["window"].tolist() == [0, 1]
```

[`chunk_plan`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.chunk_plan`) shows what a `chunk` call would produce without loading data. See [Spool chunking](../notes/spool_chunking.qmd) for how the planner works.

Data-size limits cover the array only, not coordinates, metadata, or later processing copies. `MB` is decimal and `MiB` is binary.

## Joining across seams

`chunk` joins two patches when the later starts one step after the earlier ends, give or take a fraction of a step set by `max_shift`, and then fits one evenly sampled grid to each stretch of joined patches. A wider seam is a gap, and starts a new output. `tolerance`, off by default, also joins seams up to that many steps wide (or that width, given as a quantity or timedelta) and closes them by spreading the stretch's labels evenly, as DASCore 0.1.24 did by default with `tolerance=1.5`; it warns when a joined seam is wider than 1.5 steps.

```{python}
from dascore.examples import random_spool

late = random_spool(time_gap=np.timedelta64(1_200_000, "ns"), length=2)
assert len(late.chunk(time=None)) == 2  # a seam 1.3 steps wide is a gap
assert len(late.chunk(time=None, tolerance=1.5)) == 1
```

To fill the holes `tolerance` bridges, or to report gaps and coverage, see [Large archives](large_archives.qmd#filling-bridged-holes).

## Concatenate

[`Spool.concatenate`](`dascore.Spool.concatenate`) joins each compatible group even across gaps or overlaps. Unlike `chunk`, it does not require continuity.

```{python}
earlier = dc.get_example_patch()
one_hour = dc.to_timedelta64(3600)
later = earlier.update_coords(time_min=earlier.get_coord("time").max() + one_hour)

joined = dc.spool([earlier, later]).concatenate(time=None)
```

`concatenate` can also create a new dimension when given a name not already present. Use this to stack compatible patches whose samples should remain distinct rather than merging along an existing axis.

Patches that cannot concatenate remain in separate output groups. Values are ordered along the concatenated dimension when it has a step; otherwise spool order is retained. Other coordinates must agree, while coordinates along the concatenated dimension are joined. For conflicting non-coordinate attributes, `conflict=` can raise (the default), drop them, or keep the first value.

# Loading into memory

[`Spool.load`](`dascore.core.spool.Spool.load`) reads every patch and returns a spool of in-memory patches, the way xarray's `load` does. The bytes the arrays take are estimated from the spool contents first and compared with the memory available, so a spool which will not fit raises `InsufficientMemoryError` before anything is read rather than failing part way. A patch whose size cannot be told from its metadata counts nothing. The check needs `psutil`; without it the read goes ahead unchecked.

```{python}
loaded = spool.select(distance=(0, 100)).load()
```

To load upcoming patches in the background, or apply a function to every patch, see [Large archives](large_archives.qmd#loading-ahead).

# Inventory

A spool can attach an [inventory](inventory.qmd#using-an-inventory-with-a-spool), then select and enrich patches by what it states.
